target: Prevent predictable ledger temporary paths from following, truncating or renaming pre-existing filesystem entries; allocate with create-new exclusivity and bounded collision retries while preserving deterministic successful snapshots.

baseline_observations.case: Pre-create state.tmp-<child-pid>-1 as a symlink to a sentinel victim before exec.
baseline_observations.result: The victim became asfa-directive-ledger/v4 and the final state path was a symlink to the victim.

criteria.pass: Every ledger temporary file is opened with write plus create-new exclusivity. Existing symlinks, hard links, regular files and dangling links are never followed, truncated or renamed by temporary-file allocation.

Real old/new symlink and hard-link cases reproduce baseline victim overwrite; the new binary exits 0 through a different temporary name, preserves every sentinel and pre-existing link, and leaves a regular v4 state file rather than a symlink or shared identity.

A pre-existing regular first temporary path remains byte-identical and at its original name in the new run; the new state succeeds through another name and is byte-identical to the normal control state.

After 128 pre-existing collision entries, the new binary exits nonzero with an explicit exhausted-allocation diagnostic, creates no state, and preserves all 128 entries byte-for-byte; allocation does not retry unboundedly or silently skip other I/O errors.

An independent Python oracle derives temporary names from recorded child PIDs, rechecks file types, link targets, identities and SHA-256 from the live filesystem, and rejects known-answer fake reports before accepting the real differential.

The no-collision old/new control exits 0 on both sides with byte-identical v4 snapshots and no leftover temporary path; existing output-path, wave, execution and replay fixtures remain byte-identical.
The complete gate passes and a no-.git archive of the implementation commit with an initially absent CARGO_TARGET_DIR rebuilds and repeats the real-process differential using that clean binary.

not_proven: Create-new allocation closes pre-existing temporary-entry attacks, not an adversary who can rename or replace the temporary pathname after its successful creation and before rename.
No fsync, crash-power-loss durability, WAL, hostile-OS confinement, non-cooperating-writer isolation or distributed transaction semantics are added.
No publisher authentication, zero-knowledge proof, external QF-OS/QIOS canonical compatibility, federation activation or distributed exactly-once execution is claimed.
